findings.text: Keystone Ridge is set to take over on time under W52P1J-27-C-0023: its transition-in completes Dec 22, before this contract ends Dec 31. The need is the risk that a GAO protest filed by Nov 2 stays Keystone's performance, and this contract's Oct 30 notice deadline comes before that window closes; without an extension the work would stop after Dec 31.

Performance has been acceptable: CPARS ratings were Very Good for the base period and option 1 and Satisfactory for options 2 and 3, and nine deliverables were accepted this period. The trend is down: the transition-out plan due Oct 2 hasn't arrived, and line item 0002 is past 85% of its ceiling (about 87%, not over it) with no notice from Ostrander, so raise both with Ostrander.

At the contract's rates the extension costs $290,000 a month, 4% below the follow-on's competed prices of $303,333 a month for the same line items. Line item 0002 (Data engineering support) is 19% above the follow-on's price, while the other three are 12% to 15% below it. Continuing at these rates costs far less than a gap in the work, so exercise is in the Government's best interest.

expectedOutput.reason: One month keeps the work going if the follow-on is protested and stayed, and the next notice day, Dec 2, comes after its protest window closes.
expectedOutput.summary: Extend for one month, to Jan 31, 2027, at $290,000. The follow-on can be protested until Nov 2, after the Oct 30 notice deadline, and a second decision is due Dec 2 once the window has closed.
risks: If Keystone's award isn't protested, the January extension may not be needed.
The transition-out plan is late and the ceiling notice on line item 0002 is missing.

evaluations.expectedAgentBehavior: Recommends a one-month extension. Grounds the need on the protest risk, not on the transition-in date (which is before the contract ends). Finds performance acceptable but declining, saying line item 0002 is past 85% of its ceiling, not over it. Gives the rates as 4% below the follow-on's and names line item 0002 as 19% above. Uses only the figures the facts give.

Continuing at these rates costs far less than a gap in the work, so exercise is in the Government's best interest.
